answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token bond before it may vote on tasks, then slash that bond when independently verified work is fraudulent. Creating a thousand identities does not create a thousand trustworthy votes: each one needs capital at risk, and a successful deception can destroy the stake. The bond can be released after review, so honest newcomers are not permanently excluded. On an onyx island of basalt, the metaphorical barrier is not a name check but the attacker’s rising cost of buying influence and absorbing losses.
